name: Glatiramer acetate
route_note: Subcutaneous injection 20 mg daily or 40 mg three times weekly.
targets: HLA-DR (MHC class II) binding; myelin basic protein mimicry
originator: Weizmann Institute of Science (Michael Sela, Ruth Arnon, Dvora Teitelbaum); developed by Teva
owner: Teva Pharmaceutical Industries; generic versions available

discovery.by: Michael Sela, Ruth Arnon and Dvora Teitelbaum, Weizmann Institute
discovery.note: Random copolymers made to mimic myelin basic protein and induce experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis unexpectedly suppressed it instead.

tagline: Israeli-discovered polymer injection for relapsing multiple sclerosis
summary: Glatiramer acetate is a mixture of synthetic polypeptides made from four amino acids that reduces relapses in relapsing multiple sclerosis. Discovered at the Weizmann Institute and marketed by Teva as Copaxone, it became one of the best-selling MS drugs and later faced generic competition.
mechanism: Glatiramer is a random polymer of L-glutamic acid, L-alanine, L-tyrosine and L-lysine resembling myelin basic protein. It binds MHC class II molecules and competes with myelin antigens for presentation to T cells.
It induces glatiramer-specific T helper 2 and regulatory T cells that cross into the brain and release anti-inflammatory cytokines (bystander suppression), and modulates antigen-presenting cells.
uses: Relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis, including clinically isolated syndrome

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Weizmann Institute researchers find that Copolymer 1 suppresses experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis.

history.title: First controlled trial
history.detail: Bornstein et al. (NEJM) report fewer relapses with Copolymer 1 in relapsing MS.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Copaxone is approved for relapsing-remitting MS.

history.title: 40 mg dosing
history.detail: A three-times-weekly 40 mg regimen is approved in the US.

history.title: First generic
history.detail: The FDA approves Glatopa (Sandoz/Momenta), the first generic version of the 20 mg dose; Mylan's generics follow in 2017.

history.title: Anaphylaxis boxed warning
history.detail: The FDA adds a boxed warning for anaphylaxis, which can occur years after starting treatment.

pk.half_life: not well characterised; largely hydrolysed at the injection site
pk.bioavailability: low systemic exposure as intact polymer
pk.metabolism: local hydrolysis to smaller peptides and amino acids

common: Immediate post-injection reaction (flushing, chest tightness, palpitations)
safety.boxed_warning: Anaphylaxis, which can be life-threatening and can occur shortly after any dose, including after years of treatment.

facts: Copaxone was Teva's top-selling product for many years and was central to the company's growth as a branded drug maker.
